newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean stocks continue rally on fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean stocks continue rally on fundamentals.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks continued rallying on Thursday, boosted by bullish investor sentiment on the back of positive fundamentals, dealers said.
The key 57-share industrial index leapt 84.92 points to breach the 10,000 psychological level for the second time in two weeks, ending at 10,019.03.

"The market seems to have turned around much faster than anticipated," one broker said, referring to earlier predictions by brokers that profit-taking last week, which put brakes on the exchange's month-long bullrun, may continue for a week or two.
Brokers said a lower than anticipated December inflation figure which has kept money market rates down and continuing rain were keeping investor sentiment buoyant.
Zimbabwe's annual inflation rose to 16.4 percent in December from a seven-year low of 13.9 percent in November. This was below a year-end figure of 20 percent forecast in the 1996/97 budget.
On the market on Thursday, publishing group Zimpapers surged 100 cents to 2,900 as did cigarette manufacturer Rothmans to 6,100 and clothing retailer Edgars to 4,500.

Brokers said an advisory by the central Reserve Bank on Wednesday that dual-listed stocks could now be transferred from a foreign register to the local bourse induced volatility in hotel and supermarkets group Meikles, which is also listed in London.

Meikles ended the day 75 cents up at 2,000. Tobacco company TSL rose 60 cents to 750 on the back of year-end results showing a higher dividend and share earnings while wineries Cairns gained 40 cents to 1,650 and soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes rose 30 cents to 310.

Sugar producer Hippo and cement manufacturer Circem added 25 cents each to 1,500 and 875 respectively, winery Afdis at 550 and pork processor Colcom at 450 both put on 20 cents and finance group Finhold traded 10 cents up at 850.
In minings, gold investor Falgold eased five cents to 90 after the bullion price edged below the key psychological U.S.$350 per ounce, to a fresh low fixing of U.S.$349.80.
Nickel producer Bindura shed 10 cents to 810 and the seven-counter mining index lost 9.65 points to close at 1,047.44.
